body.estimand_functional: \(\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)=\sup_{D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\leq\varepsilon}d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\), with the proved full-class bracket \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\) on each fixed bounded class containing the lower family, and the proved identity \(\Omega_{k,m}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). In the primary \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\) case, the full bracket has lower exponent \(3/4\) and upper exponent \(1/3\), while the radial exponent is sharply \(3/4\). The matching sharp full-class upper bound remains the open question \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\).

sampling_model.design: One observational environment and two grouped positive stochastic perfect-intervention environments for every latent node; group labels are observed up to one common node permutation.
sampling_model.units: \(N\) independent observations from each environment on \(\mathbb T^n\), independent across environments.
sampling_model.treatment: The environment replaces exactly one latent conditional mechanism by a parent-free circular density \(q_i^e\) normalized with respect to \(d\lambda(t)=dt/(2\pi)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every complete latent law is bounded between \(c_0\) and \(C_0\), and the decoder is uniformly bi-Lipschitz.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Positive truncated Fourier density estimation uses the vanishing floor \(\eta_N=N^{-1}\) and corrected normalization, followed by a certified finite minimum-distance fit; no derivative of an estimated density is required. The true observed densities retain the uniform lower bound \(c_0K^{-n}\). The law radius \(\rho_N\) is propagated through the proved exponent \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\), which yields \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\) in the primary case.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Then CauCA in \((G,\mathcal F,\mathcal P_G)\) is identifiable up to \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{scaling}}\).
Two hard interventions with interventional discrepancy on the same target node suffice to recover that node up to a diffeomorphism.
Then there is \(A\in SO(d)\) such that \(g^{-1}\circ f(s)=As+h(s)+b\).
Algorithms 2 and 3 are consistent estimators of the latent graph and inverse transformation up to the corresponding equivalence classes.
With a large enough \(N\), the estimated cross-derivative vectors are almost zero for all coordinate pairs.

body.tldr: Complete paired interventions yield a synthetic product law and ratio residuals. For the full bounded finite-type class, the proved inverse-modulus result is the bracket \(c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\leq\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\); the sharper upper exponent remains the arbitrary-map incompressible-rigidity question. The radial subclass is sharp at \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). In the primary two-node \(C^2\) Morse case, this means a full-class \(3/4\) lower exponent versus a \(1/3\) upper exponent, with a sharp radial exponent \(3/4\). Zero-law componentwise circular recovery follows from the direct torus identification argument, not from a converse characterization of \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}\). The certified Fourier estimator and quotient confidence-set diameter inherit the conservative exponent, giving the primary rate \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\).

project_justification.gap: CauCA and score-based causal representation learning establish componentwise exact identification under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy, but they do not metrize approximate recovery symmetrically or quantify isolated critical zeros. Quantitative Morse perturbation results requiring higher smoothness do not justify the primary \(C^2\) case, and near-isometry robustness controls a different primitive defect.
project_justification.niche: Circular latent coordinates permit a directly stated \(C^2\) Morse class and a separate finite-type hierarchy with exact uniform margins and attained worst order. Complete intervention laws add a determinant channel, while symmetric two-law quotient loss removes dependence on which competing model is declared the reference.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the synthetic product reduction, a direct zero-law torus identification result, the localized full-class lower obstruction, the conservative scalar-rigidity upper bound, the exact radial frontier, and the environment-by-environment two-node Morse audit. It also gives certified Fourier recovery and symmetric quotient confidence sets at the conservative rate, while isolating arbitrary-map incompressible rigidity as the sole step needed to close the full-class exponent gap.

body.related_work: Liang et al. establish exact CauCA recovery under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy and exhibit determinant-one rotations on common plateaus. Varıcı et al. derive componentwise and graph recovery from exact sparse score changes under paired node interventions. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\) proves the present zero-law torus conclusion directly and uses those papers only to compare assumptions and conclusion types. Neither comparator supplies a nonzero-error modulus. Buchholz and Schölkopf quantify near-isometric representation learning through a different primitive defect. Khesin et al. motivate the volume-preserving kernel, while Dacorogna--Moser and Teixeira provide prescribed-Jacobian and localized volume-correction context. Milnor supports the directly stated \(C^2\) Morse condition. Compact-manifold density and confidence-set results support the sampling rung, but the propagation exponent here comes from the proved scalar finite-type rigidity lemma.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The full-class upper exponent is presently \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\), obtained from scalar ratio residuals after the complete-law reduction. The desired exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) is proved only for the radial volume-preserving subclass. Symmetrizing the aligned loss does not supply the missing weighted incompressible coercivity, and \(d_{\mathrm{rep}}=0\) is not used as a converse test for quotient equivalence. Any counterexample to the sharper upper bound must still arise from legal complete causal law families and respect density, smoothness, conditioning, critical-separation, and attained-order bounds.
body.honest_scope: The general contribution is a full-class bracket: lower exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\) and upper exponent \(k/((k+n/2)(m+1))\). The radial restricted supremum has the sharp exponent \((k+1)/(k+m+1)\). For \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), the full bracket is \(c\varepsilon^{3/4}\leq\Omega_{2,1}(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{1/3}\), the radial rate is exactly of order \(\varepsilon^{3/4}\), and the certified estimator and confidence diameter have rate \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\). The primary class uses separated critical points and the direct Hessian bound \(|r_i''(z)|\geq a_0\), without invoking a higher-smoothness quantitative-Morse theorem. Plateaus, coalescing critical points, critical submanifolds, vector-valued contrast curves, unknown-order adaptation, and the matching arbitrary-map upper bound remain outside the proved claim.
body.interpretation: The two exponents answer different certified questions. The localized Hamiltonian family proves that no uniform full-class inverse modulus can improve on the lower obstruction \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\). Scalar finite-type rigidity guarantees recovery for every admissible decoder at the more conservative order \(\varepsilon^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\). Radial incompressibility closes this gap, but no corresponding arbitrary-map coercivity theorem has yet been proved. Thus \(3/4\) is sharp for the primary radial model and a lower obstruction for the primary full class, whereas \(1/3\) is the current full-class upper exponent.
